annotation.definitionFit: A mill stream is the channel of running water diverted to drive a watermill, so flowing water is precisely what it is.

entries.clue: Culinary paste that's semi-soft? In part (4)

indicatorNotes.In part: Taking a thing in part is taking a stretch of it rather than the whole, so the letters wanted run consecutively inside what has just been written.

entries.clue: Section of allegory that amuses youngsters (4)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a description rather than a synonym — 'the thing that amuses youngsters' — which is how a brand name gets into a sentence about literature without ever being named.

entries.clue: Basic Instinct star succeeded with character of ferryman (not the lead) (6,5)

indicatorNotes.not the lead: The lead is whoever is out in front, so the name hands itself over without the letter standing at its head.

blocks.note: s = succeeded, the abbreviation used in genealogy and in lists of monarchs

the tone of a person or a place is its character — the tone of the meeting, a shop with a certain tone

annotation.surface: A film star who came after, sharing the temperament of the boatman who rows the dead.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive is buried in 'of': the character of the ferryman is Charon's tone, and the s that makes it his is a letter of the answer. 'Character' looks like a role in a film and is a person's manner instead.

entries.clue: Something like toughly? (7)

blocks.note: approximately — the way you say something like twenty when you have not stopped to count

annotation.surface: A question about what closely resembles the word toughly.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are present at once: roughly means approximately, and to handle something roughly is to handle it toughly. On the page the two words differ by one letter, the R standing where the T was.
annotation.definitionFit: Roughly means approximately, as in roughly twenty, and it also means harshly, without care — which is toughly.

entries.clue: Declared Cockney's claim to be aware? (7)

indicatorNotes.Cockney's: A Cockney speaks with the aitches dropped, so what follows is to be taken as it comes out of the mouth rather than as it is spelt.

entries.clue: Pronouncedly idle, Everyman's of inferior quality (2-2)

entries.clue: Create moment of conception with permeating forms (10)

entries.clue: Look back to see part of castle (4)

entries.clue: Maternal protector healed mature hornet (6,6)

entries.clue: You shouldn't have tucked into pudding: not nice, ultimately lingering tang (10)

the closing letters of not and of nice, taken in that order

entries.clue: Model's not-half ugly and a little nasty on the inside: one's stuck-up (3-4)
